result:
Findings, one per test:

**`a_second_invocation_appends_and_leaves_the_first_line_intact`** — violates "expected value never comes from code under test." `lines[0]` and `lines[1]` are asserted against `event("first question").to_jsonl()` / `event("second question").to_jsonl()`, i.e. the same serialization path used to produce the data. If `to_jsonl()` is internally consistent but wrong (bad field order, wrong timestamp encoding, corrupted escaping), the test still passes. Should assert against a literal JSON string (or parsed fields with literal expected values).

**`the_first_write_creates_the_workspace_directory_it_needs`** — fine. Name matches behavior; breaking directory-creation logic turns it red; no self-derived expectation.

**`every_record_is_terminated_so_the_next_one_starts_a_new_line`** — fine, checks a literal property (`ends_with('\n')`).

**`append_returns_trail_write_failed_when_the_parent_path_is_a_regular_file`** — fine. Situation-described, hermetic (tempdir), asserts on literal substring in error detail, not derived from the code under test.

**`a_failed_write_leaves_no_partial_file_behind_for_a_reader_to_trip_over`** — fine, same setup, clear failure-mode check.

**`a_long_run_of_appends_leaves_one_line_per_invocation_and_no_torn_record`** — matches the "opt-in behind an env var, inert unless set" exception correctly. However the guard is `if var not set { return }` inside the test rather than `#[ignore]` — this makes the test silently pass (not skip) when run normally, so CI reports green with zero assertions executed. Not a standards violation per se (still inert in CI), but worth noting: a reader running `cargo test` sees "test result: ok" with no indication the body never ran. Consider `#[ignore]` + explicit `--ignored` invocation instead, for clarity, though this is a minor style point, not a rubric breach.

**Main issue to fix:** the self-consistency assertion in the second test. Everything else complies with the standards as written.
